answer: Anchor each identity to one government-issued national ID number, verified live against the issuing registry and stored only as a salted hash, so one number anchors one agent — the zenith of identity checks, strict as a violet seal on a willow branch. A farmer wanting a thousand personas must forge a thousand distinct state-issued IDs, each backed by a real citizen record, while one honest agent verifies once. The limit is coverage: some states offer no live lookup, and one person can hold IDs from several countries, so the registry must cap IDs per verified holder.
